newsitem.title: MEXICO: Jailed brother of Mexican president breaks silence.
newsitem.headline: Jailed brother of Mexican president breaks silence.

text.p: Breaking a long silence, the jailed brother of former Mexican President Carlos Salinas said a series of assassinations and kidnappings in 1994 was a conspiracy to damage the Salinas government, newspapers reported on Friday.
But Raul Salinas, speaking to reporters on Thursday for the first time since his arrest in early 1995, did not say who was behind the well-orchestrated plot.

"There was an attack on the government of Carlos Salinas in 1994," Salinas told reporters following a court hearing at the maximum security prison where he is housed. "It's not a coincidence that in that year there were all those assassinations and kidnappings of business people.
"My jailing is part of that series of events," said Salinas, who, wearing a beige prison uniform, appeared noticeably thinner than before his arrest.

Salinas made his comments following a court appearance, newspapers said. He nearly had to shout to be heard by reporters across the courtroom before a guard cut off the exchange after a few minutes, ordering the press out.
Raul Salinas, 51, referred to the tumultuous final year of his brother's 1988-1994 term as president.

After five highly successful years as president culminating with Mexico's joining the North American Free Trade Agreement with the United States and Canada, the sixth and final year of President Salinas' term became a nightmare in 1994.

A well-organized guerrilla force burst onto the scene, presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio and top ruling party official Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu were assassinated, and a prominent businessman was kidnapped for a multi-million-dollar ransom.
Shortly after Salinas gave way to current President Ernesto Zedillo in December 1994, the Mexican peso was suddenly devalued, leading to Mexico's worst economic crisis since the Great Depression.

Then, two months into his term, Zedillo ordered the arrest of Raul Salinas for masterminding the murder of Ruiz Massieu, and investigators later discovered that Salinas had stashed millions of dollars in European bank accounts, leading to illegal enrichment charges.
Prosecutors have been building both the murder and illegal enrichment cases since then.
"The file in this case has 80,000 pages and despite such a volume has yet to seriously investigate ... the intellectual authors of the crime nor Ruiz Massieu himself," Salinas said.
"Nobody knows the motive. From Pepe Ruiz Massieu, I received nothing but sensible treatment and civility. I had no motive to harm him," he added.
Ruiz Massieu was second in charge of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) when he was gunned down outside a Mexico City hotel in 1994.

Ruiz Massieu's gunman later told authorities he was hired by Congressman Manuel Munoz Rocha, a close associate of Raul Salinas who went missing shortly after the murder and was last seen heading to Raul Salinas' home.
